The query strip shows A, B, C and D in that order, so the four effects must be applied left to right to obtain the highlighted board. Every displayed gate is needed: dropping any one of them changes the result. The distractors run the gates in another order, skip one, or replace a step with another bounded primitive that fails its worked row.

puzzle.instruction: Infer how the first two boards combine, move, and turn to make the third.
puzzle.explanation: The two completed rows demonstrate the same three-part rule. First, aligned positions are combined so the output keeps positions from the first input that are absent from the second; then that result reflects left to right. Last, every arrow and triangle left on that board turns a quarter-turn clockwise where it stands, which moves no token but changes every direction. Board positions, token identities, and token directions make all three steps visible. Applying the complete rule to the last pair gives the highlighted option. Each distractor comes from another program in the same grammar that fails at least one worked row.

puzzle.instruction: Each token follows its own rule. Which board comes next?
puzzle.explanation: Read the eight outside slots as one ordered ring and follow each token separately. The circle moves 2 slots counter-clockwise and cycles outline to solid to half. The star moves 1 slot clockwise and keeps its fill. The triangle moves 2 slots clockwise and cycles outline to solid to half. Each of those rules holds across all four shown transitions, so applying all three once more gives the highlighted board. Every wrong option keeps two tokens right and steps the third by a rule that fails a transition the row already shows.

puzzle.instruction: Track how the perimeter jump changes. Where does the token land next?
puzzle.explanation: Read the eight outside slots as one ordered ring. The token moves counter-clockwise, starting with a jump of 2 slots; each later jump grows by 2. The next jump is therefore 10 slots in the same direction, which lands at the highlighted position. Each distractor comes from another bounded direction, starting jump, or growth rule that fails a shown landing.
